Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Ten-day review of metal and laboratory results, diagnosis, start of treatment, and occupational and environmental medicine consultation

text.paragraph: Ten-day review of metal and laboratory results; occupational and environmental medicine consultation today. [S]

Mr. Newton returns ten days after his first visit. He has not entered the laboratory since then; the university safety office sealed it four days ago, after measuring mercury vapor, and removed the mercury and arsenic compounds. He has moved out of the rooms next to it. He has kept the sleep diary and a fixed rising time, sleeps about four hours, and has stopped working at night, but still dozes in his chair in the evening. He eats two small meals a day. He met by chance a friend to whom he had written an odd letter and asked him to pass on his apology; he says the ideas that friends were plotting against him now seem to him to have come out of exhaustion, though he still feels slighted by one colleague. He has had no thoughts of death, of harming himself, or of harming anyone. He saw Dr. Mbeki-Lindström of occupational and environmental medicine this morning. [S]

list.item:
Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe, without psychotic features (F32.2). A year of poor sleep and appetite with 4 kg weight loss, low mood, loss of interest, poor concentration, and suspicious ideas about friends, with PHQ-9 20 then 19. Hemoglobin 14.6 g/dL, sodium 140 mmol/L, creatinine 0.92 mg/dL (eGFR 101), glucose 88 mg/dL, calcium 9.5 mg/dL, albumin 4.2 g/dL, ALT 24 U/L, TSH 1.9 mIU/L, and vitamin B12 455 pg/mL are normal, and the MoCA was 27. The suspicious ideas were never fixed, are now largely retracted, and came with no hallucinations, so there are no psychotic features and the duration and conviction do not meet delusional disorder. No manic or hypomanic episode by interview. A mercury-induced depressive disorder was considered: the urine mercury is raised, but at 46 ug/L it is below the levels ATSDR links to irritability and depression, there is no tremor, gingivitis, or erethism, and his symptoms have followed the year-long course of a depressive episode, so mercury is at most a contributor and the primary diagnosis is a major depressive episode. Dr. Mbeki-Lindström agrees. [S]
Sertraline 50 mg each morning, starting today.
Weekly cognitive behavioral therapy with the clinic psychologist, starting next week.
Collaborative care: the clinic psychiatrist reviews his scores and safety each week.
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.
If mood lifts quickly after removal from exposure alone, the diagnosis will be reconsidered.

Raised urine mercury from occupational exposure (R82.6). 24-hour urine mercury 46 ug/L (41 ug/g creatinine) and blood mercury 9.4 ug/L: real occupational absorption, in the band ATSDR links to subtle changes on nerve and psychomotor testing, without signs of toxicity. Blood lead 2.4 ug/dL is normal. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 9 mg/g and creatinine are normal. The safety office measured mercury vapor of 0.08 mg/m3 at the furnace, above the NIOSH limit of 0.05 mg/m3 averaged over a work shift. [S]
No chelation and no provoked urine test, as Dr. Mbeki-Lindström advises.
Stay out of the laboratory until it is decontaminated, re-measured, and fitted with a fume hood.
Repeat 24-hour urine mercury and blood mercury in about three weeks, and again at three months with creatinine and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.

Poor sleep, poor appetite, and suspicious thoughts (R45.89). Explained by a major depressive episode with severe comorbid insomnia, with a possible small contribution from mercury exposure; superseded by those diagnoses. [S]
Managed under the depression, insomnia, and mercury problems.

Chronic insomnia comorbid with depression (G47.00). About four hours a night; evening dozing keeps the night sleep short. [S]
CBT-I: a sleep window of 12:30 to 5:30 am, no dozing in the evening chair, out of bed after 20 minutes awake; no hypnotics.
